findings.title: State-changing unsubscribe action exposed via unauthenticated-safe GET with no CSRF protection
findings.body: The new `unsubscribe` action mutates a user's notification_level (a persisted side effect) but is only reachable via GET requests (see config/routes.rb: `get "t/:slug/:topic_id/unsubscribe" => "topics#unsubscribe"`). Rails' CSRF protection only guards unsafe HTTP verbs (POST/PUT/PATCH/DELETE); GET requests are exempt. Because the action relies on the logged-in session (`current_user`) rather than a signed token (unlike the existing `email/unsubscribe/:key` flow which uses a token), any third-party page can trigger this state change for a logged-in user simply by loading an `` tag or link pointing at this URL, silently muting/changing their topic notification preference without consent (CSRF).

findings.title: unsubscribe action can crash with NoMethodError if no TopicUser record exists
findings.body: `tu = TopicUser.find_by(user_id: current_user.id, topic_id: params[:topic_id])` can return nil (e.g. if the TopicUser row was never created, got deleted, or the user visits the unsubscribe link without a prior TopicUser record). The subsequent code immediately calls `tu.notification_level` and `tu.notification_level =`, which will raise NoMethodError on nil, causing a 500 error instead of gracefully creating/updating the record (as `TopicUser.change` would do).

findings.title: Unsubscribe bypasses TopicUser.change, losing audit fields and realtime notification
findings.body: The notification_level is updated directly on the `TopicUser` record and saved with `tu.save!`, bypassing the `TopicUser.change` class method used everywhere else in the codebase for this purpose. This means `notifications_changed_at` and `notifications_reason_id` are not updated, and the MessageBus publish of `notification_level_change` (used to keep other open tabs/clients in sync) is skipped. Because `notifications_reason_id` is left unset, later logic such as `TopicUser.auto_track` (which checks `notifications_reason_id: nil` to decide whether to auto-upgrade tracking level) may silently override the user's explicit unsubscribe choice the next time they interact with the topic.

findings.title: Template placed at wrong path for the new top-level 'topicUnsubscribe' route
findings.body: The route is registered as a flat, non-nested route: `this.route('topicUnsubscribe', { path: '/t/:slug/:id/unsubscribe' });` in app-route-map.js.es6, which (per the naming convention used throughout this codebase, e.g. the matching controller `controllers/topic-unsubscribe.js.es6` and view `views/topic-unsubscribe.js.es6`) should resolve to a template at `templates/topic-unsubscribe.hbs`. Instead the template was added at `templates/topic/unsubscribe.hbs`, which is the path convention for a nested route like `topic.unsubscribe` under the `topic` resource — a route that does not exist. This mismatch means the dedicated unsubscribe route likely renders without its intended template (blank page) or errors, defeating the purpose of the feature.

findings.title: New route path may be shadowed by existing dynamic segment route
findings.body: `this.route('topicUnsubscribe', { path: '/t/:slug/:id/unsubscribe' });` is declared after the `topic` resource, which already defines `fromParamsNear` with path `/t/:slug/:id/:nearPost`. Both patterns can match a URL like `/t/some-slug/123/unsubscribe`, with `:nearPost` capturing the literal string "unsubscribe". Depending on router/route-recognizer resolution order and specificity rules, requests to the unsubscribe URL risk being routed to `topic.fromParamsNear` instead of the new `topicUnsubscribe` route, breaking the feature or throwing an error when `nearPost="unsubscribe"` is used as a post number in `postStream.closestPostForPostNumber`.

findings.title: No tests added for the new unsubscribe controller action or Topic#unsubscribe_url
findings.body: This PR adds a new controller action (`TopicsController#unsubscribe`) that mutates notification state, a new model method (`Topic#unsubscribe_url`), and new routes, but no controller or model specs were added to cover the happy path, the nil-TopicUser edge case, the slug-mismatch redirect, or the toggle logic between regular/muted/tracking/watching. Only an unrelated mailer spec (`message_builder_spec.rb`) was minimally updated to pass an `unsubscribe_url` option.

findings.title: Misspelled property name 'stopNotificiationsText'
findings.body: The computed property is named `stopNotificiationsText` (missing an 'a', should be `stopNotificationsText`). It still works because the template references the same misspelled name, but the typo will confuse future maintainers and makes the code harder to search/grep for related functionality.
